newsitem.title: UGANDA: Uganda's Museveni rejects pay rise, allowances.
newsitem.headline: Uganda's Museveni rejects pay rise, allowances.

text.p: Uganda's President Yoweri Museveni has rejected allowances of $180,000 annually and a salary increase to save cash for educating children, government officials said on Thursday.
A government committee had recommended in February that Museveni receive $100,000 annually as a family allowance and another $80,000 for clothes.
The committee also wanted Museveni's monthly salary increased to 4.5 million Ugandan shillings ($4,205), believed to be double the current figure.
Museveni said he wanted the money to go to Universal Primary Education -- a programme that guarantees free primary education for four children per family.

Vice-President Specioza Wandira Kazibwe also rejected proposals for $135,000 in family allowances and clothes and a salary increase to 3.5 million shillings per month from an unspecified figure, government officials said.
Museveni has told economic planners that he only wanted the government to provide him with accommodation and security.
Kazibwe told a seminar in Kampala recently: "I don't need 30 pairs of shoes. I don't need a $2,000 suit."
Kazibwe said she also found the heavy security surrounding her as "rather extravagant".
Government officials said Museveni had refused to allow a 54 percent rise in the salary of members of parliament to 3.85 million shillings per month, saying it would annoy tax-payers.
The Ugandan government plans to cut spending in its 1997/98 budget due to be presented to parliament on June 12.

Museveni's stance was the latest indication of cuts in spending meant to ensure there was a supply of cash for the education programme -- one of his main campaign pledges in presidential elections he won overwhelmingly in 1995.

Museveni has also banned cabinet ministers from flying first class while on international assignment and has reduced state cars they are allowed to one per minister from two. It was not known when that order became effective.
